correctness.rationale: Every simplex not in the neighborhood-star union is proved to be one of exactly two alternating triangles per hexagon; an extra common Rips neighbor would generate a distinct six-cycle sharing an original edge. Unique midpoint paths collapse the neighborhood union to the graph. Attaching two discs per hexagon and cancelling one disc with a unique original edge yields a graph of cycle rank b-t and t null-homotopic residual disc attachments. This is an integral homotopy proof; fourteen exact finite cases corroborate the face and mod2/mod3 rank implications, not the infinite theorem.

originality.rationale: Direct full-text comparisons show the girth-seven graph-square collapse and isolated cycle calculation do not cover theta graphs carrying a hexagon and longer cycles. Metric gluing theorems for vertex/edge attachments or short overlap paths do not imply the theta(3,3,4) instance, where common overlap length three exceeds the shortest loop length divided by three. A published bipartite square-clique homological comparison is weaker and has different hypotheses. Indexed records contain examples of hexagon-rich incidence graphs but not the edge-disjoint classification.

value.rationale: This computes integral homotopy types, not only Euler characteristics or finite Betti tables, for a natural infinite graph class allowing arbitrarily many hexagons and odd cycles. The theta(3,3,4) example isolates the first noncactus mixed-dimensional behavior outside existing short-gluing theorems, and the answer explains an explicit structural mechanism by which each hexagon converts one independent graph cycle into a 2-sphere.
